decisions.decision: Phase 5 transport is peer-to-peer: every machine optionally runs the same read-only endpoint exposing its own state and lists the peers it wants to see
decisions.rationale: The user's always-on machine is the devbox, not the PC, so a PC-centred hub would leave the phone panel dead whenever the PC is off; the symmetric design also serves MOBILE-01 from the same component and keeps the single-machine experience untouched

decisions.decision: Endpoint binds the Tailscale address by default, is read-only and state-only (never transcript content); LAN fallback documented honestly; no external hosting, ever
decisions.rationale: User constraint: nothing on the public internet. Tailnet membership already provides encryption and device identity, so no per-pair key management is needed

decisions.decision: Notification ownership: visual channels (toast/flash) come from the panel you are looking at; Telegram comes only from the session's home machine
decisions.rationale: Removes duplicates by construction rather than by negotiation, and keeps phone pushes alive while the PC is off

decisions.decision: OPS-01 resolved in advance: the devbox headless instance is NOT retired — it runs its own state logic, owns its Telegram pushes, and hosts the endpoint
decisions.rationale: Follows directly from the ownership rule above

decisions.decision: Development happens on feat/* branches; main is merge-only (config git.branching_strategy=phase)
decisions.rationale: User instruction 2026-08-19 after v1.0 close put working commits straight on main
